clue.text: Puppets at the Guy Fawkes party

definitions.meaning: toy figures whose limbs jerk up when a string is pulled
small crackling fireworks that hop about, let off on Bonfire Night

explanation.surface: Puppets are on show at a Bonfire Night celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes Night (5 November) is the British Bonfire Night, celebrated with fireworks; the second definition points to the jumping firework.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a jointed toy figure worked by a string and a leaping firework.

clue.text: A massive body by Jove!

definitions.meaning: the largest planet in the solar system
Jove is another name for the chief Roman god

explanation.walkthrough: 'by Jove!' reads as an exclamation; 'by' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant planet and the king of the Roman gods share a name.

clue.text: Artificial ridicule

definitions.meaning: fake or imitation, as in imitation leather
to make fun of, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Imitation goods are sham, and to deride is to taunt.

clue.text: Notoriety of a hypochondriac

definitions.meaning: a bad reputation
playfully, the renown of someone always claiming to be sick

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into its two words: being famous for being unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepute is a bad name; a hypochondriac is known for sickness.

clue.text: Flickers like a candle along the edge of the roof

definitions.meaning: a candle flame wavers and nearly goes out

definitions.text: along the edge of the roof
definitions.meaning: channels running along the eaves to carry rainwater

explanation.definitionFit: A dying flame wavers, and rainwater channels run beneath the eaves.

clue.text: A six turning up proved to be the turning point

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of the words are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: Rolling a six in a game proves decisive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning point' seems to mean a crisis, but it is literally the line something rotates around.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaginary line about which a body rotates, like the Earth's.

clue.text: Exclusive notice

parts.note: a sign that excludes people, forbidding entry, rather than a scoop in a paper

explanation.definitionFit: A warning sign telling trespassers they are not permitted in.

clue.text: Supply teachers where the top brass are trained

definitions.meaning: read as institutions that supply the teaching staff

definitions.text: where the top brass are trained
definitions.meaning: military academies for senior officers

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a supply teacher is a temporary stand-in; here 'supply' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Institutions that provide teaching staff, and academies preparing senior officers for command.

clue.text: Preparing poultry under 14lb is work for a mason

indicators.note: in a down clue the poultry word sits below the weight

parts.note: a stone is a British unit of weight equal to 14 pounds
dressing a bird means cleaning it for cooking

explanation.surface: Getting a light chicken ready for the oven as a stonemason's job.
explanation.walkthrough: The stone, 14 pounds, is a British weight unit still used for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaping and smoothing blocks of masonry is a craftsman's task.

clue.text: Type in everything returned that is newsworthy

indicators.note: the word for type is placed inside the reversed word for everything
returned means the word for everything is read backwards

parts.note: the lot means everything
pica is a size of printing type

explanation.surface: A printer's type set among everything sent back, that being what makes the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like a verb (to type a story) but is the printer's noun, a size of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of current interest, relating to events of the day, is worth reporting.

clue.text: Poseidon's nuclear weapon?

parts.note: the sea god's three-pronged spear shares its name with Britain's submarine-launched nuclear missile system

explanation.surface: A question about whether a Greek god carries a nuclear arm.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that two worlds, Greek myth and modern weaponry, share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon's three-pronged spear and the British submarine missile system bear the same name.

clue.text: Fortune which is not THINE

annotationWithheld.why: Fortune which is not THINE: the wordplay splits the single word THINE into THIN (not thin = FAT) plus E, a split inside one clue word that the leaf grammar cannot express

clue.text: Out of fashion-except with the boys

definitions.text: Out of fashion-except with the boys

parts.words: Out of fashion-except with the boys
parts.note: the word means old-fashioned, but also describes a girl who has gone out with boys

explanation.surface: Something unfashionable everywhere except among the lads.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'out with the boys' as having been on romantic outings with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé styles are old-fashioned, while someone who went out with suitors has courted them.

clue.text: Continue being radio clown

definitions.meaning: to carry on, as a two-word phrase
a member of the cast of the zany 1950s BBC radio comedy The ... Show

explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a hugely popular British radio comedy starring Spike Milligan and Peter Sellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry on is the phrasal sense; a Goon Show performer is the comic sense.

clue.text: Bits for actors

definitions.meaning: pieces or components
roles played by performers

explanation.definitionFit: Components of a whole, and roles in a play.

clue.text: Extra payment on public transport outside

indicators.note: the word for public transport goes outside the word on

parts.note: a bus is a public transport vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bonus paid for riding the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum paid on top of usual wages as a reward.

clue.text: It is worn to correct sag in the middle

indicators.note: the word sag is placed inside the word for the middle

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garment worn to fix a sagging midriff.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a corset fixing a saggy waist, but the garment is floral, and 'the middle' is a core.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bunch of flowers pinned to a dress is worn as an adornment.

clue.text: Bawled out in the outhouse

indicators.note: the word out is placed inside the word for an outhouse

parts.note: a shed is a small outbuilding
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone yelling while in the outdoor privy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bawled out' looks like one phrase meaning scolded, but OUT is fodder going into SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to cry out loudly, synonymous with yelling.

clue.text: Bowler who tosses up seafood

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a bowler who sends the ball high in a slow arc
a large clawed crustacean eaten as a delicacy

explanation.walkthrough: A lob in cricket is a slow underarm delivery thrown high, so its bowler takes this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer who lobs the ball, and a clawed shellfish served at table.

clue.text: Key antiseptic pioneer could have treated it

definitions.text: Key antiseptic pioneer could have treated it

parts.note: B is a musical key
Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A famous surgeon could have dealt with this sore.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Lister's methods could have treated the skin sore.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluid-filled bump on the skin, the sort of wound antiseptic dressing would treat.

clue.text: Slimmer pipe-joint

definitions.meaning: a person or thing that cuts down weight
a fitting connecting pipes of different bores

explanation.definitionFit: A dieter lowers body weight; a plumbing fitting narrows from one bore to another.

clue.text: Item with which butchers tempt South African custom

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
usage means habitual practice

explanation.surface: Butchers trying to lure customers from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'custom' looks like trade from shoppers, but it is USAGE, a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger in a butcher's window is a typical product used to draw shoppers in.

clue.text: Photograph place for Highland game contest

parts.note: a shot is a photograph
to put is to place

explanation.surface: Positioning a camera to capture the Highland Games.
explanation.walkthrough: Highland Games are Scottish athletic gatherings featuring events like caber tossing and throwing a heavy ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a heavy metal ball is a classic field event at Scottish games.

clue.text: Speakers deliver it where letters are delivered

definitions.meaning: a formal speech given to an audience
the location written on an envelope

explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech, and the location mail goes to.

clue.text: Prepare to publish if the tide turns

indicators.note: turns means the word tide is read backwards

explanation.surface: Getting ready to print a paper when the tide goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise and correct text is to get it ready for printing.

clue.text: I spot one at the centre for mental treatment

indicators.note: the word for one goes at the centre of the word for spot

parts.note: a dot is a small spot
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone spotting a patient in the middle of a psychiatric unit.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-fashioned clue: the definition uses the dated clinical sense of the word for a person of very low intellect.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly a clinical label for a person deemed to need psychiatric care, now just a fool.

clue.text: March day when Caesar's side was cut

indicators.note: cut suggests the word side is chopped up and reassembled

explanation.surface: The day in March when Julius Caesar was stabbed in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar was assassinated on the 15th of March, the date the soothsayer warned him of.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar this was the 15th of March, a midmonth date.

clue.text: Handy clasp for a bag

definitions.meaning: a firm hold with the hand
a holdall or travel bag, an older sense

explanation.definitionFit: A hand's firm hold, and an old word for a travelling holdall.

clue.text: Company doctor visited by Italian lake lovers

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A firm's doctor touring a lakeside resort with romantic couples.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous lake in Lombardy, northern Italy.

clue.text: Sort of fever which sends boy to ENT

parts.note: taken as written, the hospital ear, nose and throat department
Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A fever bad enough to send a lad to the ear, nose and throat clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: Typhoid is known as the intestinal fever, from the Greek for gut.

clue.text: Professional point about beverage taking many forms

parts.note: pro is short for professional
tea is a common drink
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: An expert making a point about drinks in many varieties.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteus, the shape-shifting sea god, gives an adjective for something highly variable.

clue.text: Early measures for medicines

definitions.meaning: steps taken in advance to get ready
pharmaceutical products made up for use

explanation.definitionFit: Groundwork done beforehand, and mixtures concocted by a pharmacist.
